extraction.name: MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark
extraction.description: MTEB is a comprehensive benchmark for text embeddings spanning 8 embedding tasks covering a total of 58 datasets and 112 languages. The benchmark includes tasks such as bitext mining, classification, clustering, pair classification, reranking, retrieval, semantic textual similarity (STS), and summarization.
extraction.creator: Niklas Muennighoff, Nouamane Tazi, Loïc Magne, Nils Reimers
extraction.citeAs: Niklas Muennighoff, Nouamane Tazi, Loïc Magne, Nils Reimers. MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. arXiv:2210.07316v3 [cs.CL] 19 Mar 2023
extraction.rai:dataCollection: MTEB consists of 58 datasets covering 112 languages from 8 embedding tasks. Datasets are grouped into three categories based on text length: Sentence to sentence (S2S), Paragraph to paragraph (P2P), and Sentence to paragraph (S2P). Custom datasets were created for MTEB using public APIs from arXiv, bioRxiv, medRxiv, Reddit posts, and StackExchange posts. Other datasets were reused from existing benchmarks including BEIR, SemEval, and various other sources.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web API, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data sources include: arXiv API for scientific papers, bioRxiv/medRxiv APIs for biomedical papers, Reddit posts, StackExchange posts, Amazon customer reviews, Twitter messages, news articles, scientific papers from various domains, question-answer pairs from multiple platforms, and parallel text data for bitext mining tasks.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For ArxivClustering, BiorxivClustering, and MedrxivClustering datasets, cluster labels were generated using categories given to papers by humans. For arXiv, only the first category was used when multiple categories were assigned. Three types of clustering splits were created: main category clustering, secondary category clustering within the same main category, and secondary category clustering across all main categories. For each dataset, split and strategy, subsets of all labels were selected and articles were sampled from those labels.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For S2S datasets, the input text is the title of the paper. For P2P datasets, the input text is the concatenation of the title and abstract. MTEB imposes no limit on input length, leaving it up to models to truncate if necessary. Several clustering tasks are framed as both S2S and P2P tasks, with the former only comparing titles and the latter including both title and content.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human annotations were used for various tasks. For clustering tasks, categories were assigned by humans to papers. For classification tasks like Banking77, human annotators labeled queries with intents. For STS tasks, human assessments of sentence similarity were provided with continuous scores from 0 to 5. For summarization tasks, human annotations of machine-generated summaries were collected.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Datasets and the MTEB leaderboard are available on the Hugging Face Hub. MTEB software is available open-source at https://github.com/embeddings-benchmark/mteb. Through versioning at a dataset and software level, the benchmark aims to make it easy to reproduce results. JSON files corresponding to all results are made available together with the MTEB benchmark.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Some datasets contain sensitive attributes. MassiveIntent and MassiveScenario cover 51 languages. AmazonReviews covers 6 languages. The benchmark includes multilingual datasets covering 112 languages total, which implicitly captures language and geographic diversity.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper acknowledges that controlling for data contamination is challenging due to the scale of experiments and model pre-training. Overlap of MTEB datasets with model training datasets is ignored in MTEB scores, with the assumption that as long as enough datasets are averaged, these effects are insignificant. Some models like MiniLM and MPNet perform exceptionally well on SciDocsRR likely due to parts of the dataset being included in their training data.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: MTEB has several acknowledged limitations: (1) Long document datasets are missing - the longest datasets have only a few hundred words; (2) Task imbalance - summarization consists of only a single dataset while retrieval has 15 datasets, biasing average scores toward tasks with many datasets; (3) Multilinguality gaps - retrieval and clustering are English-only, and no code datasets are included; (4) Additional modalities are not covered - the benchmark focuses solely on natural language applications.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The benchmark is designed for evaluating text embedding models across diverse tasks including: bitext mining, classification, clustering, pair classification, reranking, retrieval, semantic textual similarity (STS), and summarization. Models can be evaluated for various use cases such as search systems, text mining, clustering and topic representation, feature representations for downstream models, and cross-lingual applications.
